subject: Permutation of posterior draws and autocorrelation

messages.author: df1e8c4ee64c5304
messages.subject: Permutation of posterior draws and autocorrelation
parts:
Back again.
I want to be sure that I understand a sentence from Gelman, Carlin, et al, Appendix 3:
"...and they are permuted so that they can be analyzed directly without concerns of autocorrelation."
But if the draws in their original order are autocorrelated (which they are likely to be), then permuting them won't change the fact that the draws aren't independent.  Unless we are actually looking for autocorrelation (or, equivalently, plotting results against "draw N"), the results of most statistical analyses won't care what the order of the posterior draws was.   Autocorrelation is taken into account in estimation of the effective sample size, and this, in turn, is used to assess MCMC error.  What about the actual parameter estimates themselves?  I imagine that, given a long enough chain, the draws do ultimately cover the distribution in a representative fashion.  That is, even if close up there is autocorrelation, the paths, broken down into pieces, are effectively random paths through the distribution space. 
Am I close to correct in the above?
Larry Hunsicker

messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Permutation of posterior draws and autocorrelation
parts:
Hi, the time that it can come up is, for example, when doing graphical posterior predictive checks, we might just simulate 20 or 100 replicated datasets and graph them.  For this purpose, you don’t want to take 20 or 100 highly autocorrelated draws.

Regarding the parameter estimates:  that’s why we compute n_eff and the Monte Carlo standard error.

A
